transcript: I had really high expectations for this new musical not just because it's Marla Mindelle’s follow up to Titanique but also because I heard a lot of hype about it beforehand so did it live up to those expectations? no no, I'm sorry to say that it didn't but I'm clearly in the minority there people are really enjoying this show I also had fun with it but I am gonna get into some thoughts so the Big Gay Jamboree shares a pretty similar premise to Schmigadoon a woman wakes up and she's trapped inside a 1940s musical comedy and it's more or less a parody of musicals from that era and we're already not off to a great start here because I gotta be honest I'm not a big fan of Schmigadoon having said that I think this musical kind of does it better in a lot of ways like it's smarter than Schmigadoon and has a bit more to say but on a basic level parodies and homages to musical theater frankly, are just not that interesting to me especially compared to the Titanique of it all where I don't think we've seen as many Titanic parodies and so it just felt a bit more novel The Big Gay Jamboree is more ambitious than Titanique though it feels bigger and has more moving parts and even though it's kind of a parody it's not an adaptation or jukebox musical so it requires just a bit more effort to pull it together into a coherent show which I think they did successfully I think where I'm getting tripped up here is a problem that I have with a lot of similar modern musical comedies with original scores if you look at Titanique or other jukebox musical comedies like it there's a lot of jokes and character humor between the songs and sprinkled into the songs but first and foremost the musical numbers are Celine Dion songs so even if something isn't laugh out loud funny you can kind of just sit back and enjoy the bop and that's kind of similar to old school musical comedies where the songs were written in such a way that they could kind of stand alone and the shows as a whole had a pretty good mix of comedy and romance and earnest charm with Big Gay Jamboree the music is very lively and energetic but it's not really designed to have a sense of musical identity of its own it's pastiche it's parody and that's fine but it means that the focus is pretty squarely on the humor everything in the show feels like it's getting us to the next laugh and even when you're extremely funny like these writers are that's a really, really difficult thing to do in musical theater because more often than not the songs feel like they're built around one central joke that you kind of get within the first 30 seconds and then the song kind of just keeps going and this problem for me is not at all unique to Big Gay Jamboree I felt the same way about a lot of other things like it but I guess I'm I guess I'm sort of the only person who is bothered by that and I still did have a good time with the show so all that to say I would still recommend it if you think it's up your alley but those are my thoughts
